name: Inspect AI
primary_layer: Contracts, control loops, scoring, and logs
environment_or_runtime: Python task, solver, and tool abstractions with sandbox integration
verifier_support: Built-in and custom scorers combining model judges and programmatic scoring
observability: Per-sample logs, events, tokens, and errors
main_limit: Not a ready-made vertical environment; task reset, domain tools, and verifiers must still be implemented

name: Harbor
primary_layer: Container execution, task adaptation, concurrency, and result normalization
environment_or_runtime: Containerized tasks with pluggable agent and benchmark adapters
verifier_support: Connects native benchmark graders and normalizes their results
observability: Run logs, resources, artifacts, and reproducible experiment metadata
main_limit: A unified entry point cannot remove environment differences or grader defects in the underlying benchmarks

name: BrowserGym
environment_or_runtime: Playwright browsers with composable observation and action spaces
verifier_support: Integrates evaluators from WebArena, WorkArena, and related suites
observability: Actions, DOM, screenshots, web pages, and error trajectories
main_limit: Primarily solves browser interaction and does not provide industry policies, permissions, or deployment governance

name: AgentLab
primary_layer: Control loops, configuration, and experiment orchestration
observability: Experiment configurations, trajectories, screenshots, and aggregated results
main_limit: Optimized scaffolds are easily conflated with model capability, and the framework is not a general vertical verifier

name: SWE-bench evaluation harness
environment_or_runtime: Builds repository images at base commits and applies candidate patches
observability: Patches, test output, container state, and evaluation logs
main_limit: Dependencies and images are brittle, while incomplete tests, task contamination, and resource differences can distort scores

name: Terminal-Bench harness
primary_layer: Container environments, agent adapters, and graders
environment_or_runtime: Isolated CLI containers with task instructions and time and resource limits
observability: Terminal trajectories, test logs, resources, and results
main_limit: Resource and network settings materially affect performance, and the terminal interface is not itself an industry rule set

name: τ-bench family runner
harness_role: Customer-service, knowledge, and voice workflow evaluator
primary_layer: User simulation, tool loops, retrieval or voice, and state verification
environment_or_runtime: Domain databases, policy documents, API tools, knowledge bases, and a user simulator
verifier_support: Target database state, communication and policy constraints, and pass^k
observability: Complete dialogue, tool calls, retrieved evidence, and terminal state
main_limit: User model, task version, turn limit, and voice conditions all change the score and therefore must be pinned and calibrated against humans

name: WorkArena / WorkArena++
primary_layer: Task setup, browser environment, and validation
environment_or_runtime: ServiceNow instances, BrowserGym, and compositional task generators
verifier_support: Programmatic terminal-state checks and oracle traces
observability: Browser actions, page state, and task logs
main_limit: ServiceNow deployment is expensive, and a single-platform template limits transfer across enterprise settings

name: AppWorld
primary_layer: Stateful world, tool contracts, and side-effect grading
environment_or_runtime: Nine simulated applications, 457 APIs, and resettable databases
observability: API trajectories, database diffs, and test results
main_limit: Simulated services omit production authentication, network failures, and API drift and do not encode a single industry's governance

name: CyberGym
primary_layer: Isolation, vulnerability reproduction, and differential verification
environment_or_runtime: Pre- and post-patch images of historical vulnerable repositories with restricted terminals
observability: Commands, build logs, crashes, and proof-of-concept artifacts
main_limit: High-risk execution needs stronger sandboxing and egress control, while a differential crash does not verify a complete attack path

name: MLE-bench
primary_layer: Data, GPU runtime, submissions, and metrics
environment_or_runtime: Isolated Kaggle competition workspaces under fixed resources
verifier_support: Competition metrics, valid submissions, and medal thresholds
observability: Code, logs, submissions, scores, and resource records
main_limit: GPU, time, and external priors are difficult to normalize, and high run cost limits multi-seed reliability evaluation

name: PaperBench
primary_layer: Containers, artifact collection, rubrics, and reproduction
environment_or_runtime: Paper-task containers with independent rerun environments
verifier_support: Hierarchical outcomes, JudgeEval, and fresh reproduction
observability: Files, command logs, rubric decisions, and reproduction results
main_limit: Expert rubrics and fresh runs are expensive, and model judges require separate meta-evaluation

name: MLGym
primary_layer: Training and evaluation APIs with continuous rewards
environment_or_runtime: Open ML tasks with code, data, and compute environments
observability: Trajectories, code changes, experiment logs, and scores
main_limit: The task count and research distribution are limited, and continuous scores can invite benchmark-specific optimization

name: OSWorld
primary_layer: Virtual-machine reset, action interfaces, and execution evaluators
environment_or_runtime: Virtual machines spanning operating systems and real desktop applications
verifier_support: Task-specific evaluators over application state, files, databases, and UI state
observability: Screenshots, accessibility trees, actions, terminal state, and errors
main_limit: Results are sensitive to virtual-machine versions, displays, and application state, and there is no built-in industry-policy layer

name: InterCode
primary_layer: Environment APIs, action loops, and task graders
environment_or_runtime: Containerized code, SQL, and shell environments
verifier_support: Execution results, tests, or target state
observability: Interaction histories, outputs, errors, and rewards
main_limit: Best treated as a terminal substrate rather than a professional-domain harness, with limited security and governance support

name: Model Context Protocol (MCP)
verifier_support: Defines return and error contracts but provides no domain verifier
observability: Protocol messages can be logged, but auditing and semantic linkage require upper layers
main_limit: The protocol is not a sandbox, trust model, or success verifier; server supply chains and permissions require separate governance

name: OpenTelemetry
verifier_support: Provides no task-correctness verifier but can carry verifier events
observability: Distributed traces, spans, metrics, logs, and baggage
main_limit: It can record only instrumented events; redaction, retention, and business semantics for sensitive trajectories must be designed separately
